comparisons.peer_summary: The company derives segment and business results using activity-based costing, funds transfer pricing, and other allocation methodologies for revenue and expense. Net interest income is adjusted to an FTE basis, resulting in a corresponding increase in income tax expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC disclose that their segment results are derived through a management reporting process involving the allocation of income and expense items to present segments as stand-alone businesses. JPM states that 'The management reporting process that derives business segment results includes the allocation of certain income and expense items,' while BAC specifies its methodology further by noting that segment results are derived by 'utilizing allocation methodologies for revenue and expense' including 'activity-based costing' and 'funds transfer pricing.' Both firms rely on internal allocation assumptions to reflect segment performance, though BAC explicitly names the specific costing models used.

sentences.text: The management reporting process that derives business segment results includes the allocation of certain income and expense items.
The management accounting and reporting process derives segment and business results by utilizing allocation methodologies for revenue and expense.

The net income derived for the businesses is dependent upon revenue and cost allocations using an activity-based costing model, funds transfer pricing, and other methodologies and assumptions management believes are appropriate to reflect the results of the business.

comparisons.peer_summary: Revenues and expenses directly associated with business segments are included in their respective operating results, while other revenues and expenses attributable to a segment are generally allocated from 'All Other' based on measures such as net revenues or non-interest expenses.
comparisons.comparison: JPM and Citi both explain that segment results are constructed by including directly associated revenues and expenses and allocating others from a central category. JPM notes that 'Results of the reportable business segments are intended to present each segment as if it were a stand-alone business' via an allocation process. Similarly, Citi states that 'Revenues and expenses directly associated with each respective business segment or component are included in determining respective operating results' while other amounts 'are generally allocated from All Other based on respective net revenues, non-interest expenses or other relevant measures.' Both use this hybrid of direct identification and allocation to define segment performance.

sentences.text: Results of the reportable business segments are intended to present each segment as if it were a stand-alone business.
The management reporting process that derives business segment results includes the allocation of certain income and expense items.
Revenues and expenses directly associated with each respective business segment or component are included in determining respective operating results.

Other revenues and expenses that are attributable to a particular business segment or component are generally allocated from All Other based on respective net revenues, non-interest expenses or other relevant measures.

comparisons.peer_topic: Segment accounting policies and allocation methods
comparisons.peer_summary: Accounting policies for segment results are consistent with Note 3, involving full allocation of revenues, expenses, assets, and equity to the three segments, with specific rules for interest income/expense, indirect expense allocation, and segment-level net earnings calculation using the firmwide tax rate.
comparisons.comparison: JPM and GS both describe a comprehensive allocation approach where all revenues, expenses, and assets are assigned to segments to reflect stand-alone performance. JPM reports that segment results involve 'the allocation of certain income and expense items' to present segments as stand-alone businesses. GS mirrors this by stating, 'The firm fully allocates its revenues, expenses, assets and shareholders' equity to the firm's three business segments.' Furthermore, both acknowledge the judgment involved in these allocations; JPM states the 'Firm periodically assesses the assumptions, methodologies and reporting classifications,' while GS admits that 'Due to the integrated nature of these segments, estimates and judgments are made in allocating these assets, revenues and expenses.'

sentences.text: Results of the reportable business segments are intended to present each segment as if it were a stand-alone business.
The Firm periodically assesses the assumptions, methodologies and reporting classifications used for segment reporting, and therefore further refinements may be implemented in future periods.
• The firm fully allocates its revenues, expenses, assets and shareholders' equity to the firm's three business segments.

• Management believes that this allocation provides a reasonable representation of each segment's contribution to consolidated net earnings to common, return on average common equity and total assets. Due to the integrated nature of these segments, estimates and judgments are made in allocating these assets, revenues and expenses. Transactions between segments are based on specific criteria or approximate third-party rates.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for MS focus on the adoption of new accounting standards (ASU 2023-07) and intersegment eliminations, rather than the specific methodology and assumptions for allocating income/expenses to derive segment results as stand-alone entities, which is the core topic of the JPM disclosure.
